A1Hazards.description: The functions where assumption A1 does not hold (`heki assumptions` lists them).

functions.description: The functions with an A1 hazard: the Soundness lane proves nothing in them.

unmodeled.description: Of those, the functions too large to model at all.

Activation.description: When a rule runs without being named by its code or name (ADR-018).

oneOf.description:
In the default selection, and matched by a prefix or `ALL`, while the rule is exact;
whatever its certainty with `lint.heuristic`.
Only by its exact code or name.

Selected as an exact `Default` rule is, whatever its certainty: it reports only what a
declared contract asks for, so declaring the contract is what selects it.

Analyzed.description: The files the report was computed from.

errors.description: The files that could not be read or parsed, as `heki check` reports them.

functions.description: The functions in them, module bodies included.

paths.description: The paths given on the command line.

catalog_may_miss.description:
Names of packages the catalog covers that it has no entry for, which `heki check` would
report if they waited or sent a query: at most 50.

source_roots.description:
Directories that resolve imports naming no project module once they are source roots,
the most imports first: at most 50.

truncated.description: Whether a list holds fewer entries than there are.

uncatalogued.description:
The calls of names of packages the ecosystem catalog does not cover, by package, the
package with the most reach first: at most 50.

unresolved.description:
The calls heki resolves to no function, by function and reason, the most reach first: at
most 50.

CauseRow.description: The reports that leave one premise or condition open for one cause.

cause.description: The cause, unique within its premise or condition.

closer.description:
What closes the cause: `annotation` (an annotation the user writes, which must be
true), `code` (a change of the code's shape), `heki-catalog` (a fact only heki's
shipped catalog can hold), or `none` (nothing the user can apply to every case).

examples.description: The first 50 reports, in report order.

name.description: The premise's name in the premise table (docs/precision.md), or the condition's.

only_open.description: The reports it is the only open premise or condition of.

reports.description: The reports that leave it open.

rules.description: The reports by the exact rule whose claim they report.

CauseRule.description: The reports of one rule's claim that leave a cause open.

rule.description: The exact rule whose claim the reports state.

Closer.description: What closes an open cause, for every case the cause stands for.

oneOf.description: An annotation the user writes; heki trusts it under R2, so it must be true.
A change of the code's shape.
A fact only heki's shipped catalog can hold (no `[[tool.heki.ecosystem]]` key sets it).

Nothing the user can apply to every case: heki cannot establish the premise today, the
code states the opposite, or the cause stands for cases with different closers that the
facts do not tell apart yet.

Combination.description: Causes that reports leave open together.

oneOf.description:
The trial found nothing the contract cannot see: no access it cannot tie to a class (an
effect boundary: no scope function reaching code heki does not see), and every Python file
below the project root was analyzed.

The trial reports no violation, but heki may not see all the contract is about: accesses
on objects of unknown class, Python files below the project root left out, or scope
functions reaching code heki does not see. The caveats say which. An ownership entry then
sets `unresolved = "ignore"`.

Consequence.description: What happens in the code a rule reports, which sets its default severity.

oneOf.description:
A bug that can be critical: a wrong result, an exception, a lost update, a deadlock, or a
broken contract.

A bug that is rarely harmful: a promise the code makes is broken, such as a read-only
annotation, where the callers seldom notice.
Slower code that computes the right result.

ContractAdvice.description: A candidate the trial kept: the block declares it.

caveats.description: What the confidence does not cover.

entry.description: The entry the block declares, as the keys it sets.

target.description:
What the entry is about: the attribute (`module:Class.attr`), or the package or module its
scopes cover.

trial.description: What the contract trial reported for it.

ContractKind.description: The kinds of contract `heki recommend` proposes, by their key in the configuration.

Counts.description: How many calls there are, and what they may hold up.

awaited.description: The calls that are awaited: whatever they run, they do not hold up the event loop.

in_loops.description: The calls inside a loop of their function, or in a function below a loop.

on_event_loop.description:
The calls, not awaited, in a function on an event loop (an `async def`, or a function
one runs on its thread): one that waits holds the loop up.

Evidence.description: What a candidate rests on, from the discovery run.

audience.description:
The other modules reading the attribute (`write-owners`), using its class
(`read-owners`), or calling into the scopes (`effect-boundaries`).

functions.description:
The functions the entry allows (`write-owners`: those writing the attribute after its
object is constructed; `read-owners`: those reading it) or holds (`effect-boundaries`:
the functions its scopes' modules define, without the comprehensions and lambdas inside
them), fully qualified.

in_place.description: `write-owners`: a writer changes the attribute's object in place (a container).

modules.description:
The modules of those functions; for an attribute written only while its objects are
constructed, the module of its class.

unseen.description:
`effect-boundaries`: the functions of the scopes reaching code heki does not see (a call
it does not resolve, a library name without a catalog entry, an A1 hazard, a body known
only from a stub).

name.description: The module or name the import names.

LeftOut.description:
The Python files below the project root that the paths given leave out: heki takes the
files it analyzed as the whole project.

files.description: The files found, in the order of a walk of the root sorted by name.

python_files.description: How many were found (when `truncated`, a lower bound).

truncated.description:
Whether the count stopped before the end (after 50 files, or after the first 10,000
entries below the root) or could not read an entry.

Listed.description: A list of names, the first [`MAX_LISTED`] of them.

NotTried.description:
The candidates of one kind past the first [`MAX_CANDIDATES`] (for `write-owners`, less the
configuration's own), which no trial declared.

OpenKind.description:
What a report leaves open: a premise of its claim, which may then be false, or a condition
of the exact tier that is no premise, under which the claim holds.

OpenPremises.description: The heuristic reports of exact claims, by what keeps them heuristic.

by_cause.description:
One row per premise or condition left open and cause, the row that is the only open one
of the most reports first, then the row of the most reports.

by_rule.description: Those reports by the code they are reported under, the most first.

combinations.description:
The sets of more than one cause that reports leave open together, the commonest first:
at most 50.

not_recorded.description: The reports that record no cause, by code: they are counted under no row of `by_cause`.

reports.description:
The heuristic reports of exact claims, as `heki check` prints them with every rule
selected: the heuristic reports of the exact rules.

truncated.description: Whether `combinations` holds fewer sets than there are.

PackageCalls.description: The calls of the names of one package.

awaited.description: The calls that are awaited: whatever they run, they do not hold up the event loop.

in_loops.description: The calls inside a loop of their function, or in a function below a loop.

on_event_loop.description:
The calls, not awaited, in a function on an event loop (an `async def`, or a function
one runs on its thread): one that waits holds the loop up.

symbols.description: The names called, the one with the most reach first.

PublishedMeasurement.description:
A measurement as published: the classes of the sampled reports, and the shares derived
from them.

benign.description: Reports that are right, of code that is deliberate or harmless at realistic sizes.

confirmed.description: Reports whose problem is real and observable from the code.

date.description: The date of the build the round measured.

false_claims.description: Reports that are wrong about the code.

plausible.description: Reports that are right, of code that does harm at realistic sizes.

real_harm_percent.description: The share of real harm (confirmed and plausible), in percent.

right_percent.description: The share right about the code (confirmed, plausible, and benign), in percent.

round.description: The round of the measurement protocol.

RejectedContract.description: A candidate a run with it declared reported for.

entry.description: The entry the block would declare.

run.description:
The run that reported it: the contract trial, or the verification run with the whole
block.

target.description: What the entry is about, as for a candidate kept.

ReportAt.description: One report, with where it leaves the cause open.

at.description: Where the premise or condition is open: the call of a chain's hop, or a loop.

detail.description: What the cause's statement leaves out: the function, value, or class it is about.

ReportsNow.description:
What the current configuration shows, as `heki check` prints it: reports that share a root
cause are folded into one.

baseline.description: With a baseline: the reports it allows, and the regressions `heki check` prints.

heuristic_rules_off.description: The heuristic rules that are off only because `lint.heuristic` is false.

shown.description: The reports `heki check` prints without a baseline.

withheld_heuristic.description: The heuristic reports of exact rules that `lint.heuristic = false` leaves out.

RuleAdvice.description: One rule the current selection does not run in full.

baseline.description: With a baseline: the added reports it allows, and the regressions.

enabled_now.description:
Whether the current selection runs the rule: then only its heuristic reports, which it
withholds, are counted.

in_block.description: Whether the block enables the rule.

measurement.description: The latest published measurement of how often the rule's reports are right.

reason.description: Why the rule is in the block or not.

reports.description:
The reports naming the rule in `extend-select` would add to what `heki check` prints
(`null` for a rule that is not counted).

oneOf.description: Every rule selected, on the configuration as it is.

The source-root trial: the module names of the files with directories added to `src`,
and the imports they resolve (no analysis).

The configuration with a catalog entry that waits and sends a query for each library
name tried, and the rules those effects make report.
The configuration with every contract candidate declared, the contract rules selected.
The configuration with the whole block applied, the block's rules and contracts selected.

SourceRoot.description: A directory that, made a source root, resolves imports that name no project module now.

imports.description: The imports of its files that name no project module now.

in_block.description: Whether the block adds it to `src`.

reason.description: Why it is in the block or not.

SymbolCalls.description: The calls of one library name.

awaited.description: The calls that are awaited: whatever they run, they do not hold up the event loop.

if_queries.description:
The `EFF103` reports `heki check` would print if the call sent a database query (`null`:
not tried).

if_waits.description:
The `EFF101` reports `heki check` would print if the call waited on the network, from
the hypothetical-catalog run (`null`: the name was not tried).

in_loops.description: The calls inside a loop of their function, or in a function below a loop.

on_event_loop.description:
The calls, not awaited, in a function on an event loop (an `async def`, or a function
one runs on its thread): one that waits holds the loop up.

symbol.description:
Spelled as an entry of `[[tool.heki.ecosystem]]` needs it: entries are looked up by this
exact name, without inheritance or aliases.

below_source_roots.description:
The calls of names below a directory of `source_roots`: calls of the project's files,
which the library names leave out.

not_tried.description: The library names it did not: past the first 64 by reach.

registered_calls.description: The calls of names of packages the catalog covers, without an entry.

source_root_candidates.description: The directories of `source_roots`, those past the first 50 included.

tried.description: The library names the hypothetical-catalog run gave an entry.

uncatalogued.description: The calls of names of packages the catalog does not cover.

unresolved_functions.description: The functions making a call heki resolves to no function.

unresolved_groups.description: The groups of those calls by function and reason.

Trial.description: What a run with the contract declared reported for it.

examples.description:
The reports after inline suppressions, the first 50 in the order `heki check` prints
them.

reports.description:
The reports after inline suppressions, by rule: the contract's rule, and for an ownership
contract the rule of the accesses it cannot tie to a class.

TrialReports.description: The reports of one rule the hypothetical-catalog run printed, by certainty.

UnmatchedEntry.description:
A contract entry that matches nothing in the analyzed files, with every contract of its kind
holding the same text under the same key.

contracts.description:
The contracts holding it, in configuration order: a name, or `#<position>` (from 1) for
a contract without one.

named_at_run_time.description:
The class family gets attributes named at run time, which may include the entry's:
heki cannot tell whether it names one (judged only with
`unmatched-contract-entries = "error"`).

names_no.description: What it names none of, in the words of the message (`function or method`).

nearest.description:
Existing names like the entry, written as the entry is, the closest first (at most
three).

UnresolvedCalls.description: The calls one function makes that heki resolves to no function, for one reason.

awaited.description: The calls that are awaited: whatever they run, they do not hold up the event loop.

in_loops.description: The calls inside a loop of their function, or in a function below a loop.

names.description: The methods and names called, each once, sorted.

on_event_loop.description:
The calls, not awaited, in a function on an event loop (an `async def`, or a function
one runs on its thread): one that waits holds the loop up.

parameter.description: The parameter, for a reason about one.

description: The JSON object `heki recommend --output-format json` prints.

blind_spots.description: What heki cannot see: no count of reports applies there.

config.description: The keys `config_toml` adds or changes, as the configuration's keys and values.

config_file.description: The configuration file the run read, or `null` when the project has none.

config_toml.description: The keys to add or change, as TOML for `config_file` (empty when nothing is added).

content.description: The report as the text output prints it.

contracts.description:
The contracts the code keeps, which the block declares: each kept by the contract trial,
then applied with the whole block by the verification run. By kind, then by rank within
it.

contracts_not_tried.description: The candidates past the cap of their kind, which no trial declared.

heki.description: The version of heki that wrote the report.

notes.description: What the reader should know to weigh the advice.

open_premises.description: What keeps the heuristic reports of exact claims heuristic.

rejected_contracts.description: The candidates a run with them declared reported for: not in the block.

root.description: The project root, as the output writes paths (`.` for the working directory).

rules.description:
Every rule the configuration does not run in full: the rules it leaves off, and the exact
rules whose heuristic reports it withholds. The block's rules come first.

runs.description: The analyses the report was computed from, in the order they ran.

table_prefix.description:
The table the configuration's keys are under in that file: `tool.heki` in a
`pyproject.toml`, empty for a file that holds them at its top level (`heki.toml`).

unmatched_entries.description:
The entries of the contracts configured now that match nothing in the analyzed files, one
per kind, key, and text, in configuration order.

version.description:
The version of the object's fields: it changes when a field is removed or changes
meaning; fields are only added within a version.

title: heki recommend
